angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 349,937 km at 66.29 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.0852 +/- 0.0093 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 66.29 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.503 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Mann et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-1651 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract): 349,937 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.522 +/- 0.033 solar masses from Mann et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-1651 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3713 +/- 57 K from Mann et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1651 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mann et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1651 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..267M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-1651.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.753, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
